# Different model formulation

## Load data

we use the reduced dataset for this section

Quick reminder: this dataset contrains 16 samples with balanced number of female and males. Only one experiment is included.

```{r}
se <- readRDS("./datasets/small_vHC.rds")
```

## Female as baseline 

Firstly, we set Female as reference level of the Sex.

```{r}
se_F <- se
colData(se_F)$Sex <- factor(colData(se_F)$Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")) # set Female as the reference level
se_F <- se_F[, order(colData(se_F)$Sex)]

table(se_F$group)

dge <- DGEList(assay(se_F, "counts"))
mm <- model.matrix(~ Sex * Condition, data=as.data.frame(colData(se_F)))
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)
keep <- filterByExpr(dge, mm, min.count = 10)# Filter out lowly expressed genes (less than 10 reads)
dge <- dge[keep, ]
se_F <- se_F[rownames(dge), ]# Subset SE to only filtered genes
```

```{r}
set.seed(16)
tmp <- SEtools::svacor(se_F, ~  Sex * Condition, numSVmethod = "be", method = "vst") # suggested 2 SVs
tmp <- SEtools::svacor(se_F, ~  Sex * Condition, numSVmethod = "leek", method = "vst")

se_F <- SEtools::svacor(se_F, ~ Sex * Condition, n.s = 2)
# pp <- plotMDS(assay(se_F,"corrected"), plot=FALSE)
# mds <- cbind(as.data.frame(colData(se_F)), x=pp$x, y=pp$y)
# ggplot(mds, aes(x,y,shape=Sex,colour=Condition)) + 
#   geom_point() +
#   labs(title = "MDS: 2 Surrogate variables")
```

```{r}
# Compute log2FC changes relative to Ctrls. This assay will later be used for visualization
se_F <- log2FC(se_F, "corrected", controls = grep("Ctrl", se_F$group), isLog = TRUE)

# create an edgeR object, storing count data and associated sample information
dge <- DGEList(assay(se_F))
# The model contains Sex and Condition, and their interaction, and the surrogate variables (SVs)
formula <- as.formula(paste(c("~ Sex * Condition", grep("^SV[0-9]+$",colnames(colData(se_F)),value=TRUE)), collapse="+"))
mm <- model.matrix(formula, data = as.data.frame(colData(se_F)))
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)  # calculate TMM normalization factors to correct for differences in library composition between samples
dge <- estimateDisp(dge, mm) # estimate dispersion

# Fit quasi-likelihood negative-binomial models
fit <- glmQLFit(dge, mm, prior.count = 0.5)
assay(se_F, "logcpm") <- log1p(cpm(dge)) # calculate logcpm for later visualization

Results_stress_F <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit,coef = "ConditionStress"),Inf))
# Results_stress_F selects "ConditionStress"
# Answering the question: is there any Stress effect in Females (becase Female is the reference sex) 
# This is often misinterpreted as general stress effect across sexes.

Results_interaction_F <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "SexMale:ConditionStress"),Inf))
# Results_interaction_F only tests the interaction of Sex and Condition
# Answering the question: does the Stress effect differs between sexes

Results_both_F <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit,coef = c("ConditionStress", "SexMale:ConditionStress")),Inf))
# Results_both_F selects both ConditionStress and SexMale:ConditionStress
# Answering the question: does Stress matter at all, either as a "main" effect or through its interaction with Sex
```

```{r}
stress_degs_F <- rownames(Results_stress_F[Results_stress_F$FDR < 0.05,])
interaction_degs_F <- rownames(Results_interaction_F[Results_interaction_F$FDR < 0.05,])
stress_interaction_degs_F <- rownames(Results_both_F[Results_both_F$FDR < 0.05,])

# Renaming for visualization
se_renamed_F <- se_F
rownames(se_renamed_F) <- sub(".*\\.", "", rownames(se_renamed_F))
stress_degs_renamed_F <- sub(".*\\.", "", stress_degs_F)
```

### Fig 3A

```{r}
fig3a <- sechm(
  se = se_renamed_F, 
  feature = stress_degs_renamed_F, 
  gaps_at = c("Condition"), 
  assayName = "scaledLFC", 
  top_annotation = c("Condition", "Sex"),
  anno_labels = TRUE, 
  anno_label_gp = list(size = 10, col = "white"),
  column_title = NULL,  
  use_raster = TRUE,
  show_heatmap_legend = FALSE,
  show_annotation_legend = FALSE
)
fig3a
```

```{r}
# Optional: check stress DEGs signature in boxplot
sexLogFC_stressSignature_plts(se_F, stress_degs_F, "Stress", "Stress")
```

## Male as baseline 

In this section, we reset Male as reference level of Sex, and apply the same DEA as above.

```{r}
se_M <- se
colData(se_M)$Sex <- factor(colData(se_M)$Sex, levels = c("Male", "Female"))  # here we set Male as the reference level

dge <- DGEList(assay(se_M, "counts"))
mm <- model.matrix(~ Sex * Condition, data=as.data.frame(colData(se_M)))
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)
keep <- filterByExpr(dge, mm, min.count = 10)# Filter out lowly expressed genes (less than 10 reads)
dge <- dge[keep, ]
se_M <- se_M[rownames(dge), ] # Subset SE to only filtered genes
dge <- estimateDisp(dge, mm) # estimate dispersion
```

```{r}
set.seed(1)
tmp <- SEtools::svacor(se_M, ~  Sex * Condition, numSVmethod = "be", method = "vst")  # suggested 2 SVs
tmp <- SEtools::svacor(se_M, ~  Sex * Condition, numSVmethod = "leek", method = "vst")

se_M <- SEtools::svacor(se_M, ~ Sex * Condition, n.sv = 2, method = "vst")
# pp <- plotMDS(assay(se_M,"corrected"), plot=FALSE)
# mds <- cbind(as.data.frame(colData(se_M)), x=pp$x, y=pp$y)
# ggplot(mds, aes(x, y, shape = Sex, colour = Condition)) + 
#   geom_point() +
#   labs(title = "MDS: 2 Surrogate variables")
```

```{r}
se_M <- log2FC(se_M, "corrected", controls = grep("Ctrl", se_M$group), isLog = TRUE)  # calculate the logFC (Stress vs. control)
dge <- DGEList(assay(se_M))
formula <- as.formula(paste(c("~ Sex * Condition", grep("^SV[0-9]+$",colnames(colData(se_M)),value=TRUE)), collapse="+"))
mm <- model.matrix(formula, data = as.data.frame(colData(se_M)))
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)
dge <- estimateDisp(dge, mm)
assay(se_M, "logcpm") <- log1p(cpm(dge))
fit <- glmQLFit(dge, mm)

Results_stress_M <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "ConditionStress"),Inf))
# Now Results_stress_M answers the question: is there any Stress effect in Males (becase Male is the reference sex) 

Results_interaction_M <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "SexFemale:ConditionStress"),Inf))
Results_both_M <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, coef = c("ConditionStress", "SexFemale:ConditionStress")),Inf))
```

```{r}
stress_degs_M <- rownames(Results_stress_M[Results_stress_M$FDR < 0.05,])
interaction_degs_M <- rownames(Results_interaction_M[Results_interaction_M$FDR < 0.05,])
stress_interaction_degs_M <- rownames(Results_both_M[Results_both_M$FDR < 0.05,])

# Rename for visualization
se_renamed_M <- se_M
rownames(se_renamed_M) <- sub(".*\\.", "", rownames(se_renamed_M))
stress_degs_renamed_M <- sub(".*\\.", "", stress_degs_M)
se_renamed_M$Sex <- factor(se_renamed_M$Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male"))
se_renamed_M <- se_renamed_M[, order(se_renamed_M$Condition, se_renamed_M$Sex)]
```

### Fig 3B

```{r}
fig3b <-  sechm(
  se = se_renamed_M, 
  feature = stress_degs_renamed_M, 
  gaps_at = c("Condition"), 
  assayName = "scaledLFC", 
  top_annotation = c("Condition", "Sex"),
  anno_labels = TRUE, 
  anno_label_gp = list(size = 10, col = "white"),
  column_title = NULL, 
  use_raster=TRUE
)
fig3b
```

# Different model formulation slop plot (fig 3C)

This plot compare the three approaches: Female-baseline model, Male-baseline model, Reference analysis. 

```{r}
ref <- readRDS("./objects/reference_analysis_obj.rds")  # results from reference analysis. See reference_analysis.Rmd and section 2.6
SE_ref <- ref$se
DEGs_ref <- names(ref$DEGs$MF_stress_degs_filtered)

df_ref <- get_logFC_df(SE_ref, DEGs_ref, "Reference")
df_M <- get_logFC_df(se_M, stress_degs_M, "Male baseline")
df_F <- get_logFC_df(se_F, stress_degs_F, "Female baseline")

combined_df <- rbind(df_ref, df_M, df_F)

common_genes <- intersect(stress_degs_M, stress_degs_F)
common_genes <- sub(".*\\.", "", common_genes)
combined_df$color_group <- ifelse(combined_df$gene %in% common_genes, 
                                 "Male \u2229 Female", 
                                  as.character(combined_df$dataset))

fig3c <- ggplot(combined_df, aes(x = males, y = females)) +
  geom_point(data = subset(combined_df, dataset != "Reference"), 
             aes(color = color_group), size = 0.7, alpha = 1) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "gray40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray40") +
  xlab("log2FC (Males)") +
  ylab("log2FC (Females)") +
  ggtitle("Stress DEGs of Different Model Formulations") +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(),
    legend.title = element_blank()
  ) +
  geom_smooth(method = MASS::rlm, 
              method.args = list(formula = y ~ 0 + x),
              aes(group = dataset, color = dataset), se = F, fullrange = TRUE) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Reference" = "#DC3220", 
                                "Male baseline" = "#E1BE6A", 
                                "Female baseline" = "#40B0A6",
                                "Male \u2229 Female" = "gray30"))

fig3c
```

# Permutation (fig 3D)

We repeatedly subsample the original data to evaluate whether the baseline-dependent bias observed above is stable. For each permutation, we randomly subsample, then fit a female-baseline model and a male-baseline model, respectively, then compare the resulting genes as above.

```{r}
se <- readRDS("./datasets/whole_vHC_dataset.rds")
table(se[,se$Experiment %in% c("Privitera.E2", "vonZiegler.E3")]$group)
```

```{r}
set.seed(1234)

exp_configs <- list("Privitera.E2" = 13, "vonZiegler.E3" = 2)
n_samples_per_group <- 3

# Reading analyzed dataset
ref <- readRDS("./objects/reference_analysis_obj.rds")
SE_ref <- ref$se
DEGs_ref <- names(ref$DEGs$MF_stress_degs_filtered)

rownames(SE_ref) <- clean_name(rownames(SE_ref))
DEGs_ref <- clean_name(DEGs_ref)

# Calculate Reference Stress Coef
df_ref <- calculate_stress_coef(SE_ref, DEGs_ref, "Reference\n")

# Initialize a list to store results of each permutations
permutations <- list()

# --- 2. PROCESSING ---
for (exp_id in names(exp_configs)) {
  
  se_exp <- se[, se$Experiment == exp_id]
  n_perms <- exp_configs[[exp_id]]
  idx_list <- split(seq_len(ncol(se_exp)), se_exp$group)
  
  # Optional: report the process
  # message(sprintf("\n--- Processing Experiment: %s (%d permutations) ---", exp_id, n_perms))

  for (i in 1:n_perms) {
    # Optional: report the progress
    # message(sprintf("Running Permutation %d/%d...", i, n_perms))
    
    # Subsampling
    selected_idx <- unlist(lapply(idx_list, function(x) sample(x, n_samples_per_group)))
    se_perm <- se_exp[, selected_idx]
    
    # Batch Correction
    suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(invisible(capture.output(
      se_perm <- SEtools::svacor(se_perm, ~ Sex * Condition, n.sv = 1, method = "vst")
    ))))

    # Calculate log2FC on corrected counts
    se_perm <- log2FC(se_perm, "corrected", controls = se_perm$Condition == "Ctrl")
    
    # edgeR
    dge <- DGEList(assay(se_perm, "counts"))
    dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)
    coldata_perm <- as.data.frame(colData(se_perm))
    
    # --- Male Baseline Model ---
    mm_m <- model.matrix(~ Sex * Condition + SV1, data = coldata_perm)
    dge <- estimateDisp(dge, mm_m)
    fit_m <- glmFit(dge, mm_m)
    res_m <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmLRT(fit_m, coef = "ConditionStress"), Inf))
    m_degs <- rownames(res_m[res_m$FDR < 0.05, ])
    # print(length(m_degs))  # optional: report DEG number
    
    # --- Female Baseline Model ---
    coldata_f <- coldata_perm
    coldata_f$Sex <- factor(coldata_f$Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male"))
    mm_f <- model.matrix(~ Sex * Condition + SV1, data = coldata_f)
    # We reuse the dispersions from dge and re-fit the releveled model
    fit_f <- glmFit(dge, mm_f)
    res_f <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmLRT(fit_f, coef = "ConditionStress"), Inf))
    f_degs <- rownames(res_f[res_f$FDR < 0.05, ])
    # print(length(f_degs))  # optional: report DEG number

    rownames(se_perm) <- clean_name(rownames(se_perm))
    
    # --- Coefficient calculation ---
    df_male <- calculate_stress_coef(se_perm, clean_name(m_degs), "Male\nBaseline") 
    df_female <- calculate_stress_coef(se_perm, clean_name(f_degs), "Female\nBaseline")
    
# Add metadata to identify the source of these rows
    df_male$Permutation <- i
    df_male$Experiment <- exp_id
    df_female$Permutation <- i
    df_female$Experiment <- exp_id
    
    # Append to the list
    permutations[[length(permutations) + 1]] <- df_male
    permutations[[length(permutations) + 1]] <- df_female
  }
}

# Combine all permutation results into one data frame
df_all_perms <- do.call(rbind, permutations)

# Ensure the Reference data frame has the same columns for binding
df_ref$Permutation <- 0
df_ref$Experiment <- "Reference"

# Stack Reference at the top followed by all permutations
final_df <- rbind(df_ref, df_all_perms)

# Optional: View the structure
print(head(final_df))    

```

## Fig 3D

```{r}
# 1. Define global limits
# Calculate the min and max across the entire dataset so both plots share the exact same scale
global_limits <- range(final_df$coefficient, na.rm = TRUE)
label_height = 1.5

# 2. Set shared theme
common_theme <- list(
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.4),
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8), 
             size = 1.5, shape = 21, color = "black", stroke = 0.5),
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", alpha = 0.6),
  stat_compare_means(aes(group = Sex), method = "t.test", label = "p.signif", label.y = label_height),
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Male" = "#E1BE6A", "Female" = "#40B0A6")),
  theme_bw(),
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
)

# 3. Plot Reference analysis (Individual Sample Coefs)
p_ref <- subset(final_df, dataset == "Reference\n") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Condition, y = coefficient, fill = Sex)) +
  facet_wrap(~ dataset) + 
  common_theme +
  # Force the Y-axis to the global range
  coord_cartesian(ylim = global_limits) + 
  labs(
    y = "Stress LogFC Curve Slope (Per Sample)", 
    x = NULL
  )

# 4. Plot Permutation results (Means)
p_perm <- subset(final_df, dataset != "Reference\n") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Condition, y = coefficient, fill = Sex)) +
  facet_wrap(~ dataset) +
  common_theme +
  # Force the Y-axis to the same global range
  coord_cartesian(ylim = global_limits) + 
  labs(
    y = "Group Average Stress LogFC Curve Slope\n(Per Permutation)", 
    x = NULL
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(l = 10)), # Add space for the label
     axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )

fig3d <- p_ref + p_perm + 
  plot_layout(guides = "collect", widths = c(1, 2)) + 
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Stability of the Baseline Bias across 15 Sample Permutations",
    subtitle = "Stress LogFC Curve Slope of the Reference versus Baseline Models"
  )

fig3d
```
